items.argument: Booking-time ensureAvailableUsers checks recurring working hours but does not enforce dateOverrides. A restrictive override skipped by the stated timezone defect can therefore permit an actual booking, bypassing a permitted booking window.

Ordinary booking creation rechecks weekdays, but handleNewBooking.ts skips ensureAvailableUsers for seat-enabled events, a supported configuration. The wrongly offered slot can therefore become a booking with a fixed host outside their working days.

Booking-time validation does not enforce date overrides. The incorrectly retained slot can pass recurring working-hours checks and be booked on a day explicitly marked unavailable, establishing an admission-control bypass.
The booking handler skips its full-slot working-hours recheck for seat-enabled events. In that supported configuration, the incorrectly offered slot can be accepted beyond the host's working hours.

The unsubscribe action deterministically crashes for an ordinary valid user state: no TopicUser row. That makes an identified supported path unusable for those users; the affected cohort does not lower severity.
The stated production asset failure affects the shared embed layout, making the embed path unusable under precompiled assets. It is not confined to one embed record.

The same incompatible geometry is passed on every attempt through the automatic-downsize path. Taking the claimed failure as true, valid oversized images cannot receive the promised resizing; this disables a supported operation rather than describing one defective image.

For clients with a resource, administrators relying on the global grant cannot complete operations gated by hasPermission(ClientModel, String). This meets the exception for wrongful denial that makes a supported path unusable; it does not require all administration to fail.

The described mechanism leaves offsets uncommitted; it does not mark unprocessed work complete. Dropping the in-memory queue therefore supports redelivery and reprocessing, while 'or loss' supplies no concrete mechanism for systemic destructive loss.

The comment explicitly claims exploitable byte-by-byte secret recovery followed by arbitrary users' credential overwrites. Under the instruction to assume its claims are true, that supplies the critical consequence; accepting that stated exploit does not invent exploit success.

The comment gives a concrete validation path that accepts superseded recovery codes for login, bypassing the replacement authentication factor. The supplied definition does not require a prerequisite-free attack; possession of an invalidated code does not make it a currently authorized factor.
